1) Trigger rule: if by 2026‑08‑03 no vendor demonstrably meets all required acceptance conditions—(a) HIL or representative simulation/archived‑data showing mission‑level low‑RCS detection/track improvements over baseline (mission‑meaningful margin; e.g., PD uplift and track‑loss reduction demonstrated with objective metrics), (b) proven datalink/API interoperability with legacy radars and coalition standard in integration tests, (c) instrumented operator testing showing measurable workload reduction and effective automated cueing, and (d) a documented cyber‑accreditation/ATO path with no unresolved show‑stopper findings—then the acquisition will pivot.

3) Evaluation criteria (what CO must collect): objective PD/track continuity metrics, interoperability test logs/APIs, validated operator workload data (e.g., NASA‑TLX or equivalent), vendor cyber artifacts and ATO schedule, and vendor technical/cost/schedule estimates for integration. 
4) Time‑boxed execution: Contracting will run the final evidence collection through 2026‑08‑03; Program Office will simultaneously prepare the modular, performance‑based SOW and procurement package to enable immediate award if pivot is required.
